title: "Mortality"

Mortality statistics describe deaths in a population during a stated period. This page establishes the public explanation that will be completed when the BNR mortality specifications and outputs are approved.

::: {.callout-note title="Publication status"}
BNR mortality products are in development. No provisional formula or source rule on this holding page should be treated as an approved BNR measure.
:::

## What mortality measures can tell us

Common measures include:

- the number of deaths;
- the crude death rate relative to the resident population;
- age-specific death rates;
- age-adjusted death rates for comparison; and
- the distribution of deaths by cause.

## Decisions to record before publication

The completed specification will state:

| Element | To be confirmed |
|---|---|
| Population | Residence rules and period covered |
| Death definition | Registered deaths and any registration-delay rules |
| Cause | Underlying or contributing cause and the coding system used |
| Denominator | Population source and release |
| Adjustment | Age groups, standard population and interval method |
| Revisions | Treatment of late registrations and cause corrections |

## Mortality is not case fatality

Mortality uses the population as its denominator. [Case fatality](case-fatality.qmd) uses eligible CVD events as its denominator. The two measures therefore answer different questions.

## What to remember

The final page will be completed before BNR mortality figures are described as routine public measures.
